papers.title: A Little Advice Suffices: Diffie-Hellman Is as Hard as Discrete Logarithm
papers.abstract: Is computing a Diffie-Hellman key as hard as computing a discrete logarithm? Maurer showed that it is, given a few bits of advice, provided that short intervals contain enough integers with only small prime factors; that proviso has stood for thirty years. We remove it. For every prime $p$ there is an advice string of $O(\log p)$ bits, depending only on $p$, with which discrete logarithms in every group of order $p$ are computed in polynomial time from a Diffie-Hellman oracle. The reduction is the classical one; what was missing was a proof that short intervals contain polylogarithmically smooth integers. We show that a zero-free half-plane for the Riemann zeta function, which is now known, gives the expected number of $(\log x)^K$-smooth integers in every interval $[x,x+x^\theta]$ with $\theta>17/30$. With smoothness this small the saddle point of the counting integral lies just to the left of the line $\mathrm{Re}\,s=1$, and a zero-free strip of any fixed width absorbs the shift once $K$ is large. Genus-2 Jacobians, whose orders fill such intervals, then turn one of these integers into the order of an auxiliary group. The same input removes the smoothness assumption from Maurer and Raub's impossibility of field-homomorphic one-way permutations and from the yes/no-query reduction of Koblitz, Menezes and Shparlinski. It also makes Wolf's characterisation unconditional: discrete logarithm and Diffie-Hellman are generically equivalent exactly when the group order has no large repeated prime factor.

papers.title: Reduction Modulo Binary Polynomials with Logarithmic Feedback Depth
papers.abstract: Polynomial modular reduction is central to binary finite-field arithmetic and repeated Frobenius powering. Top-down shift/XOR folding can use few operations when the nonleading support is sparse, but a tap near the leading term creates a long feedback chain. We formulate this recurrence as inversion of a nilpotent shift operator and factor its inverse by characteristic-two Frobenius powers. The resulting Frobenius-factorized reduction (FFR) applies to every monic binary modulus without materializing a reciprocal or dense reduction matrix, and its shifts can be generated online without a persistent modulus-specific schedule. For degree $m$ and nonempty nonleading support of size $s$, with nearest-tap distance $\Delta_{\min}$, FFR uses exactly $\lceil\log_2(m/\Delta_{\min})\rceil$ sequential feedback stages and has scheduled work $O(ms(1+\log(m/s)))$. A portable-C evaluation on 1,096 supports through degree $131072$ identifies distinct FFR, L\'opez--Dahab, and gf2x-backed Barrett regions. On four certified irreducible moduli, FFR makes complete Rabin irreducibility testing $1.35$--$8.04$ times faster than NTL and $1.60$--$6.81$ times faster than the matched Barrett implementation.

papers.title: The Nygaard graded piece, the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and regularity criteria
papers.abstract: For a $p$-torsionfree $p$-quasisyntomic ring, we construct a fiber sequence relating the $p$-th Nygaard graded piece of absolute prismatic cohomology to the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex. The latter is an arithmetic analogue of the cotangent complex in which the differential of $p$ need not vanish. We also clarify the relationship between the regularity criterion proved by Mao using the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and the regularity criterion established by Bhatt and Mathew using the Nygaard graded piece. This relationship was anticipated by Bhatt and Mathew.

papers.title: The injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties over imaginary quadratic fields under some lattice hypotheses. We express integrals of the lift over special cycles as special values of Dirichlet series and deduce injectivity by separating the Fourier coefficients of the cusp forms. We also establish a converse theorem for Borcherds products on $\mathrm{U}(n,1)$.

papers.title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly. In this paper we close this gap and determine the system of length sets when the class group is isomorphic to $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$.

papers.title: Bounded functions on the character variety for quadratic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
papers.abstract: For any finite extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, Schneider--Teitelbaum defined and studied the character variety in $p$-adic Fourier theory. It is a rigid analytic curve over $L$ that parameterizes the set of locally $L$-analytic characters of $o_L$. It is conjectured that all bounded functions on the character variety of Schneider--Teitelbaum come from $p$-adic measures. We prove this conjecture for all quadratic extensions $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$.

papers.title: A local-local principle for quadratic forms over semiglobal fields
papers.abstract: Given a quadratic form over a semiglobal field, the set of discrete valuations on the field for which the form is anisotropic over the completion is either empty, or it contains a valuation extending that of the base field with a transcendental residue field extension. In dimension at least $3$, this gives a refinement of the local-global principle for isotropy. In dimension $2$, the result yields a description of the set of elements that are locally squares everywhere.

papers.title: An application of "Selmer group Chabauty" to arithmetic dynamics
papers.abstract: We describe how one can use the "Selmer group Chabauty" method developed by the author to show that certain hyperelliptic curves of the form $$ C \colon y^2 = x^{2g+1} + h(x)^2 \,, $$ with $h \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ such that $\operatorname{deg} h \le g$ and $h(0)$ is odd, have only the "obvious" rational points $\infty$ (the unique point at infinity on the smooth projective model of the curve) and $(0, \pm h(0))$. Let $c \in \mathbb{Q}$ and write $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$. We denote the iterates of $f_c$ by $f_c^{\circ n}$; i.e., we set $f_c^{\circ 0}(x) = x$ and $f_c^{\circ(n+1)}(x) = f_c(f_c^{\circ n}(x))$. As an application of the method, we prove that if $f_c^{\circ 2}$ is irreducible, then $f_c^{\circ 6}$ is also irreducible. Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), it also follows that $f_c^{\circ 10}$ is irreducible.

papers.title: Greatest Common Divisors and an Unlikely Intersection Type Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove inequalities involving greatest common divisors of functions at integral points with respect to numerically parallel divisors, generalizing a result of Wang and Yasufuku (after work of Bugeaud-Corvaja-Zannier, Corvaja-Zannier, and the second author). In addition to proving results in a broader context than previously considered, we also study the exceptional set in this setting, for both the counting function and the proximity function. Based on our study of exceptional sets, we propose new conjectures connected to the topic of unlikely intersections. We prove special cases of the conjectures on abelian varieties and the algebraic torus, including a completely explicit result in the former case, and provide a link between the conjectures and exceptional sets for inequalities involving greatest common divisors.

papers.title: On the V-toothpick sequence
papers.abstract: We give a generating function for the V-toothpick sequence and an algorithm that computes any term in time polynomial in the number of binary digits of its index. We determine its quadratic growth and periodic fluctuations, and give convergent series for the constants in its asymptotic bounds.

papers.title: Klarner's sequences have density $0$
papers.abstract: We prove that the set of non-negative integers $n$ which can be obtained from $0$ by repeated application of affine maps $x\mapsto 2x$, $x\mapsto 3x+2$ and $x\mapsto 6x+3$ has density $0$. Moreover, we reach the same conclusion for five other sequences of similar type introduced by D. Klarner. More generally, we establish a criterion excluding stationary measures with bounded density on the profinite group $\mathbb Z_P\cong\prod_{p\mid P}\mathbb Z_p$. A density-to-measure construction using invariant Banach limits and a combinatorial argument involving rational orbits and affine words yield our density-zero results. The criterion also applies to an infinite family of mixed-slope affine semigroups.

papers.title: Tilings of integer sets of prime-power cardinality
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a finite integer tile of cardinality $p^k$, where $p$ is prime and $k\geq1$. We first determine all possible fundamental periods of tilings of $A$. A cyclotomic argument gives a common period $PD$, where $P$ is a power of $p$ and $D$ is a greatest common divisor of normalized differences in $A$. Each $Pd$ with $d\mid D$ occurs as a fundamental period. At modulus $Pd$, a chain of greatest common divisors controls the compatibility of the Chinese remainder fibres. This yields independent digit functions and exact counts of the tilings. For tilings of fundamental period $Pd$, we classify their partitions into translates modulo $Pd$ and count the tilings that induce each partition. The same arithmetic data classify tiles with identical tiling families. Each class has a unique normalized tile of minimum diameter whose mask polynomial divides the masks of all normalized tiles in the class.

papers.title: $\ell^p$-Improving for Discrete Fractional Integrals and Averages on the Moment Curve
papers.abstract: We prove the $\ell^p$-improving estimates in the full range for discrete fractional integral operators on the moment curve (except at the endpoint) and discrete averages on the moment curve (with $N^{\epsilon}$-losses). This follows via essentially sharp Diophantine solution counting estimates for inhomogeneous Vinogradov systems with an odd number of variables.

papers.title: Asymptotic statistics for finite continued fractions with restricted digits
papers.abstract: Zaremba's conjecture concerns a formation of continued fraction expansions for rational numbers with partial quotient bounded by an absolute constant. We present asymptotic estimates for the size of $\epsilon$-thickening of certain fractal sets of bounded-type, which in turn provide a remark on Zaremba's conjecture in an averaging sense. We also discuss a generalisation for complex continued fractions over imaginary quadratic fields.

papers.title: Strong Approximation for the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere
papers.abstract: We study the orbits of solutions to the Markoff-type equation $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + AX + BY + CZ + D$$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$ for fixed integers $A,B,C,D$ under the group $\Gamma$ generated by \[\begin{split}&V_1: (x, y, z)\mapsto (A + yz - x, y, z),\\ &V_2: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, B + xz - y, z),\text{ and}\\ &V_3: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, y, C + xy - z).\end{split}\] This equation defines the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere, with $\Gamma$ arising from the Pure Mapping Class Group. Outside an explicit degeneracy locus, $\Gamma$ acts transitively on almost all solutions for a density-one set of primes independent of the parameters; the others split into small orbits reflecting finite orbits over $\mathbb{C}$. For ``degenerate'' parameters, we show there are two large orbits (most cases) or four (the rest, excluding $(0, 0, 0, 4)$) for the same primes. These results strengthen for two subfamilies. The first, $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + k,\,\,\,k\neq 4,$$ arises in the combinatorial group theory of $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$. Combined with Chen's work, $\Gamma$ acts transitively for all large primes, uniformly in $k$, so the $Q$-classification conjecture of McCullough and Wanderley holds over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for $p$ large. By Martin's work, so do their Classification and $T$-Classification Conjectures. The second, $$x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 + a_1x_2x_3 + a_2x_1x_3 + a_3x_1x_2 = (3+a_1+a_2+a_3)x_1x_2x_3,$$ arises from generalized cluster algebras. Our degeneracy notion specializes to that of de Courcy-Ireland, Litman, and Mizuno, whose results similarly imply our orbit count (1, 2, or 4) for all large primes for all nondegenerate and some degenerate surfaces in that family.ds for all sufficiently large primes.

papers.title: The Hofstadter Consecutive-Sum Sequence Omits Infinitely Many Positive Integers
papers.abstract: We study Hofstadter's greedy self-generating sequence, which begins with 1 and 2 and repeatedly chooses the least integer larger than the preceding term that is a sum of at least two consecutive earlier terms. We prove that the excess of its $n$th term over its index is bounded below by a positive constant times $\log\log n$, up to an additive constant, and that the sequence satisfies a polynomial upper bound. In particular, the sequence omits infinitely many positive integers.

papers.title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $\rho\colon G\to \mathrm{GSp}_{2n}(\mathbb Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity-free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $\Gamma_\rho^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ associated with $\rho$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $\rho$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by a $G$-stable symplectic lattice. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\mathrm{GSp}_{2n}(\mathbb Q_p)$, we prove, under suitable assumptions, the existence of certain paths in $\Gamma_\rho^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ and show that $\Gamma_\rho^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.

papers.title: $L^p$-norms of holomorphic cusp forms
papers.abstract: We determine the optimal orders of local and global $L^p$-norms of $L^2$-normalized holomorphic cusp forms of large weight on the modular surface, for fixed $2<p\leq\infty$. Both orders are attained by peak forms. For normalized Poincar\'e series of weight $k$ and index $m$, we obtain an asymptotic formula with an explicit constant, uniformly for $1\leq m\leq c_0k$ with any fixed $c_0<(4\pi)^{-1}$. We also give sup norm bounds in a wider range of indices.

papers.title: Abelian varieties with homotheties
papers.abstract: In 1980, Bogomolov proved that the $\ell$-adic Galois image of an Abelian variety over a number field contains an open subgroup of the homotheties. In 1986, Serre refined that result, showing that the homotheties coming from the Galois side were uniformly bounded in $\ell$ inside the homotheties of the codomain of the representation. In a 2007 paper, Zarhin shows that Bogomolov's conclusion can fail in non-trivial cases for global function fields. We prove a suitable analogue of Serre's results over finitely generated fields of positive characteristic. As a consequence, we prove a new case of the 1978 conjecture by Geyer and Jarden.

papers.title: The totient bound and extremal gaps in cyclotomic polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $m>1$ be odd and squarefree, and let $p\nmid m$ be prime. If $p<m$, every gap in $\Phi_{mp}$ has length strictly less than $\varphi(m)$. If $p>m$, the maximum gap has length $\varphi(m)$ and occurs exactly $2\lfloor p/m\rfloor$ times. We determine its positions and endpoint coefficients. These results prove the equality criterion of Ambrosino, Hong and Lee and the multiplicity formula of Zhang. We also treat repeated prime factors, even cofactors and extremal zero runs in periodic coefficient blocks.

papers.title: Invariant flags and integral matrices with prescribed characteristic polynomial
papers.abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for integral matrices with a prescribed characteristic polynomial in an expanding entry box over a number field. For cyclic matrices, normalized logarithmic covolumes of a primary invariant flag become uniform on a permutohedral chamber. Their joint distribution with the rescaled matrix factors for tests invariant under reflections at the real places. Separating irreducible factors of multiplicities \(e_i\) into distinct translates multiplies the leading coefficient by \(\prod_i e_i!\). We also bound every noncyclic rational type.

papers.title: Congruence Patterns in Spectral Gaps of mod $p$ Markoff Graphs
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the second-largest eigenvalue of mod $p$ Markoff graphs for three infinite, positive-density families of primes $p$, each defined by congruence conditions. These lower bounds arise from the structure of integral orbits on Markoff-type surfaces over certain number fields, and are strong enough to establish that $$\liminf_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv1\pmod{4}}}\lambda_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.875> 2\sqrt{2},$$ partially proving a conjecture of de Courcy-Ireland and Lee, and that $$\limsup_{\substack{p\rightarrow\infty\\p\equiv 3\pmod{4}}}(\lambda_2(\Mar^*(\F_p)) > 2.835 > 2\sqrt{2},$$ disproving another conjecture of the same.

papers.title: Invariant distributions and common denominators in the Bernstein center
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field. We conjecture that every invariant distribution whose support is compact modulo conjugation belongs to the rational Bernstein center. We also make an explicit conjecture about the ideal of possible denominators (the description is using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and involves working with endoscopic subgroups of $G$). We prove this for products of general linear groups; in this case the above idea is much more explicit and Langlands correspondence is not needed for its description (it is a principle ideal, where the generator is given by some version of the discriminant function). We also prove our general conjecture for $G=\mathrm{SL}(2)$.

papers.title: On Ext-groups between Arthur-type modules of the graded Hecke algebras of type A
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb H_n$ be the graded Hecke algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. This article establishes a formula for Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and a $W$-type $\mathbb H_n$-module in terms of Littlewood-Richardson coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain an explicit and efficient method to compute Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and an Arthur-type module of $\mathbb H_n$. In particular, this proves new instances of a conjecture of Chan and Prasad on Ext non-vanishing between Arthur-type representations. We also discuss some other non-Ext vanishing results for calibrated modules.

papers.title: A Normal Form for Invertible Semilinear Maps and the Category of Isocrystals Over a Finite Field
papers.abstract: For a field $L$, and a finite order automorphism $\sigma$, we classify invertible $\sigma$-semilinear endomorphisms on finite-dimensional $L$-vector spaces up to equivalence. This is deduced as a consequence of a description, in terms of certain norm equations in finite extensions of $L$, of the semilinear Schur indices for the group $\mathbb{Z}$ acting on $L$ via $\sigma$. As an application, we give an explicit description of the category of isocrystals over a finite field.

papers.title: On a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture via categorical representations
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a complex reductive group. For a smooth affine spherical $G$-variety $X$ such that the stabilizer of a point in the $B$-orbit under the $B$-action be connected, assume that the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture of Ben-Zvi-Sakellaridis-Venkatesh (BZSV) for $X$ holds. We establish a spectral description of a full subcategory of Iwahori equivariant coherent D-modules on $LX$ in terms of the relative Langlands dual of $X$, confirming a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture proposed by Devalapurkar.

papers.title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_\mu$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.

papers.title: The Constant in Thomae-Type Formulas for Eight Points on the Complex Projective Line
papers.abstract: We consider the family of cyclic fourfold covers $C(x)$ of the complex projective line branched at eight points $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_8)$. It is known that the period map identifies the configuration space $X(2,8)$ of the branch points with a Zariski open subset of a quotient of the five-dimensional complex ball, and that the inverse of the period map is expressed projectively by $105$ automorphic forms $f_J$, which are proportional to the signed branch-point polynomials $\hat x_J$ with a common scalar factor. We normalize an element $\omega$ of the one-dimensional eigenspace of the deck transformation group acting on the holomorphic differentials on $C(x)$. For the period $\eta$ of $\omega$, we determine the common scalar factor: it is the product of a constant expressed in terms of the gamma function and the square of a quadratic form in $\eta$.

papers.title: Infinite Derivatives and Local Extrema of the Delange Function of Every Base
papers.abstract: For an integer $q\ge2$, the Delange function of base $q$ is $T_q(x)=\sum_{j=0}^\infty q^{-j}\tau_q(q^jx)$, where $\tau_q$ has period $1$, is linear on $[k/q,(k+1)/q]$ for integers $0\le k<q$, and satisfies $\tau_q(k/q)=k(q-k)/q$ for $0\le k\le q$. Thus $T_2$ is Takagi's function. In the Hamming graph on $\{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}^n$, two words are adjacent exactly when they differ in one letter. For integers $n\ge1$ and $0\le m\le q^n$, $q^nT_q(m/q^n)$ is the smallest number of edges leaving a set of $m$ vertices, which is known. We characterize infinite derivatives by the base $q$ digits $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$ of $x\in[0,1)$. Outside the $q$-adic rationals $m/q^n$ with integers $m$ and $n\ge0$, the right derivative is $+\infty$ exactly when $\sum_{j=1}^n(q-1-2\xi_j)\to+\infty$. The condition for the left derivative to be $+\infty$ also involves the lengths of the maximal strings of zeros. For $-\infty$, the sides and the digits $0$ and $q-1$ are exchanged. The local minima are exactly the $q$-adic rationals. The local maxima are exactly the points $(m+u)/q^n+k$ with integers $k$, $m$, $n$ such that $n\ge0$, $0\le m<q^n$, and the base $q$ digit sum of $m$ is $(q-1)n/2$, where $u$ maximizes $T_q$ on $[0,1]$. For odd $q$, we have $u=1/2$ and every local maximum is strict. For even $q$, there are uncountably many such $u$ and no local maximum is strict. We also find the maximum on each interval $[m/q^n,(m+1)/q^n]$ and all points attaining it. For an integer $h$ with $1\le h\le q^n/2$, we determine the minimum number of edges whose deletion disconnects the graph into components with at least $h$ vertices, including a digit criterion for equality with the minimum boundary at size $h$. Almost every level set $\{x\in[0,1]:T_q(x)=y\}$ is finite, whereas the level set through almost every point is uncountable. Here almost every refers to Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: Estimates for the Number of Solutions of Algebraic Diophantine Equations: From the Circle Method to the Manin Conjecture
papers.abstract: This work continues the research of the author on estimates for the number of solutions of algebraic diophantine equations by means of the circle method and develops this line in the geometric direction, towards counting integral points on log Fano varieties. It consists of two parts. Part 1 is the corrected version of the previous work. For diagonal equations $c_1x^{k_1} +...+c_sx^{k_s} = n$ with natural coefficients, upper asymptotic estimates for the number of natural solutions in the range $s \leq 2^k$, where the classical asymptotics is not applicable, are obtained by the circle method and the Hua lemma. The estimates are refined for $s = 2,3,4$ and various $k_i$; in the range $s > 2^k$ they agree with the classical ones. Part 2 develops the same line: from counting solutions of equations to counting integral points on log Fano varieties, where the circle method fails because of insuf ficient dimension. In the log case, the product in the Peyre constant diverges as a harmonic series. A method of analytic compensation is introduced that cancels the divergent term and returns the problem to the range of applicability of the standard scheme. The main result is a method for computing the Peyre log constant with guar anteed accuracy and certified intervals for the number of integral points whenever an estimate of the remainder of the asymptotics is known. The log constant is computable unconditionally, without the Manin conjecture; the conjecture is needed only to interpret it as the leading term of the asymptotics. An experimental verification for the algebraic torus and the Fermat cubic surface is presented.
